PLEASE READ CAREFULLY before attempting this quiz!

Do NOT attempt to do this assessment on a mobile device or on the Pulse App - it will not work properly! Please access this quiz via eips.brightspace.com using a chromebook, laptop, or some sort of PC.

This is intended to be a closed book quiz. The only accessible resources that should be available to you during the quiz is the Biology 30 Datasheet. Marks received on this quiz will be recorded on PowerSchool but will not count towards your overall grade in the course. 

You will have only 1 attempt to do this quiz, so do not start it until you are absolutely ready. Once it is started you will have two hours to complete it. Any responses after the time is up will NOT be recorded.

Be sure everything is saved and SUBMITTED before the time is up!
Your quiz has been submitted successfully.
If 75 percent of the offspring from many experimental crosses showed only the dominant phenotype, then you would infer
that both parents were homozygous dominant.
that one parent was homozygous dominant and the second parent was homozygous recessive.
that both parents were heterozygous.
that one parent was homozygous recessive, and the second parent was heterozygous.
Combinations of alleles such as (GGTT) and (ggtt) occur on a single pair of chromosomes before meiosis. How might you explain a combination of (Gt) or (gT) in the gametes?
sex linkage
lack of dominance
non-disjunction
crossing over
A test cross is used to determine
the phenotype of the parent
the genotype of the parent
the phenotype of the offspring
if independent assortment occurred

Identify the phenotypic ratio of F2 plants, if all the F1 plants had a “TtYy” genotype.

a.   9: 3: 3: 1

b.   3: 1

c.   1: 1: 1: 1

d.   1: 1
9: 3: 3: 1
3: 1
1: 1: 1: 1
3: 3: 1: 1
The genotypic and phenotypic ratios for the F1 plants are:
all TTRR; all are tall plants that produce red flowers
all ttrr; all are dwarf plants that produce white flowers
all TtRr; all are tall plants that produce red flowers
all TtRr; all are tall plants that produce pink flowers
The mode of inheritance expressed in this cross is
polygenic inheritance in one pair of genes, and complete dominance in the other pair of genes
incomplete dominance in both pairs of genes
incomplete dominance in one pair of genes, and complete dominance in the other pair of genes
polygenic inheritance in both pairs of genes
In humans, pointed eyebrows (B) are dominant over smooth eyebrows (b). Mary’s father has pointed eyebrows, but she and her mother have smooth eyebrows. What is the genotype of the father?
BB
Bb
bb
BBbb
Parents who do not have Tay-Sachs disease (autosomal recessive) produce a child that has Tay-Sachs. What are the chances that each child born to this couple will have Tay-Sachs disease?
100 percent
75 percent
25 percent
0 percent
Lise and Henri are at the opposite extremes for a polygenic trait. Their children will
be homozygous recessive for all of the alleles
be a phenotype typical of a 9: 3: 3: 1 ratio
have the middle phenotype between their two parents
look like one parent or the other
Which of the following statements is true with respect to this pedigree chart?
Wavy hair is dominant to straight hair.
Individuals I-1 and I-2 are homozygous.
Individual II-2 is homozygous.
If individuals II-1 and II-2 have more children than the ones shown, these children might have straight hair.
Based on this pedigree chart, you could infer that the inheritance of hair texture is an example of
incomplete dominance
multiple alleles
an autosomal recessive trait
a sex-linked, recessive trait

In persons with sickle-cell disease, the red blood cells are shaped like a “sickle” and are not biconcave disks like normal red blood cells. Mr. and Mrs. Charleson are both carriers (HbAHbS) of sickle-cell disease. What are the chances of their having a child with sickle-cell disease?
0 percent
25 percent
50 percent
100 percent
Which of the following would be the genotypic and phenotypic ratio of the F1 individuals?
9 widow’s peak and short fingers: 3 widow’s peak and long fingers; 3 straight hairline and short fingers: 1 straight hairline and long fingers
1 widow’s peak and short fingers: 1 widow’s peak and long fingers: 1 straight hairline and short fingers: 1 straight hairline and long fingers
1 widow’s peak and short fingers: 1 straight hairline and long fingers
all widow’s peak and short fingers.
In this same hypothetical situation, two F1 generation individuals are crossed. What is the probability of the F2individuals having a widow’s peak hairline and long fingers?
A mother and daughter have PKU. The son does not have PKU. What is the genotype of the father?
AA
Aa
aa
cannot be determined from the information provided

A woman who is heterozygous for Huntington’s disease marries a man who is homozygous recessive. What is the probability that this couple will have a child that will eventually develop Huntington’s disease?
0 percent
25 percent
50 percent
75 percent
100 percent

The feather colour in some species of chickens is governed by two dominant alleles (co-dominance). Black birds are homozygous for the B allele and white birds are homozygous for the W allele. Predict the phenotype of the F1generation when a black rooster is crossed with a white hen?
100 percent of the chicks will have black and white plumage.
50 percent of the chicks will have black plumage and 50 percent of the chicks will have white plumage.
100 percent of the chicks will have grey plumage.
50 percent of the chicks will have black and white plumage, and 50 percent of the chicks will have grey plumage.

In fruit flies the gene for eye colour is found on the X chromosome. In these flies, red eye colour is dominant to white-eye colour. Predict the probability of producing white-eyed male offspring in a cross between a female fly that is homozygous for red eye colour and a male fly that has white eyes.
100 percent of the male offspring will have white eyes.
75 percent of the male offspring will have white eyes.
25 percent of the male offspring will have white eyes.
0 percent of the male offspring will have white eyes.

The dominant (R) allele produces red coloured fruit in tomatoes, while the recessive (r) allele produces yellow fruit. The dominant (P) allele produces a purplish coloured stem in tomatoes, while the recessive (p) allele produces a stem with a green colour. Predict the phenotypic ratio of F1 plants, when the P1 genotypes are RrPp × rrpp.

What is the probability (in percent) of two parents with type A blood (heterozygous) having a child with type A blood?

 

(Record your two-digit answer with no spaces or commas below - example 12)

The P1 cross is between a full colour male (D1 D3) and dilute colour female (D2 D3).

 

Calculate the theoretical probability of producing the F1 phenotypes shown below. 

 

(Record your answers as full percentages separated by : for each phenotype - example 25:50:25)

Calculate the map distance between the genes for eye colour and wing type.

 

(Round your answer to one decimal place, and record your three-digit answer with no spaces below - example 12.3)

What is the probability that another male child born to individuals II-1 and II-2 will be colour blind?

 

(Record your answer as a whole percentage below - example 50)

In the first cross, a rabbit with the chinchilla coat colour is mated to a rabbit with a Himalayan coat colour that is known to be homozygous for this trait. Calculate the theoretical probability of this cross producing each of the following phenotypes shown below.

(Record your answer as a full percentage for each phenotype separated by : as shown in order below - do not include spaces or percent signs - example 25:25:0:25:25)

In the second cross, a full colour rabbit (CCa) is mated to a light grey rabbit (CchCa). Calculate the theoretical probability of this cross producing each of the following phenotypes shown below.

(Record your answer as a full percentage for each phenotype separated by : as shown in order below - do not include spaces or percent signs - example 25:25:0:25:25)
Which of the following statements best describes the inheritance of an X‑linked dominant disorder?
A man who has the disorder has a 0% chance of passing it on to his son.
A man who has the disorder has a 50% chance of passing it on to his daughter.
A woman who is heterozygous for the disorder has a 100% chance of passing it on to her son.
A woman who is heterozygous for the disorder has a 100% chance of passing it on to her daughter.

If two Labrador retrievers with the genotype BbEe were to be crossed, what phenotypic ratio would be expected in their offspring?
 
(Record your three-digit answer with no spaces or commas below - example 123)

Legend Gene Pairs Cross-over Frequencies

2  Ovarian cancer 1 and 3 12%
3  Rh blood group 2 and 3 9%
4  Ragweed sensitivity 2 and 4 19.5%

The order in which the four genes listed in the legend above are located on chromosome 6 is _____, _____, _____, and _____.
